body_text: A new Oxford University study suggests modern poultry farming may be accelerating the spread of Campylobacter, increasing concerns about food poisoning, antibiotic resistance, and public health. Food safety experts have long warned consumers about the risks of handling and eating undercooked chicken. Now, new research suggests that changes in modern poultry farming may be contributing to the spread of Campylobacter , a bacterium responsible for thousands of food poisoning cases each year and linked to serious health complications. Researchers from the University of Oxford have found evidence that the movement of Campylobacter between wild birds and commercial chicken flocks has increased dramatically over recent decades. Their findings suggest that intensive poultry production may be creating conditions that help harmful bacteria spread, evolve, and develop resistance to antibiotics. While the study does not conclude that commercial chicken directly causes cancer, it highlights concerns about foodborne infections, antibiotic resistance, and the importance of maintaining strong food safety practices. Oxford Study Examines Campylobacter Evolution The research, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) , analyzed 2,747 Campylobacter samples collected from commercial chickens and wild birds across 30 countries over a period spanning more than four decades. By studying the bacteria's genetic makeup, scientists discovered that Campylobacter has become increasingly adapted to life inside commercial poultry flocks. According to the researchers, the exchange of bacteria between wild birds and farmed chickens has increased significantly over time. Larger poultry populations provide more opportunities for bacteria to circulate, exchange genetic material, and evolve into strains that may be harder to eliminate. The researchers describe this as an example of how human driven environmental changes can influence the evolution and spread of infectious diseases. Why Campylobacter Matters Campylobacter is one of the leading causes of bacterial food poisoning worldwide. In the United Kingdom, it is estimated to cause around 70,000 infections every year , although many experts believe the actual number may be considerably higher because not every case is reported. Most infections occur after people consume undercooked poultry or foods contaminated through cross contamination during food preparation. Common symptoms include: Diarrhea Stomach cramps Vomiting Fever Nausea Blood in the stool in some cases Most healthy adults recover within a week without requiring specific treatment. However, severe infections can occur, particularly among: Older adults Young children Pregnant women People with weakened immune systems In rare cases, Campylobacter can enter the bloodstream, leading to sepsis , a life threatening medical emergency. Commercial Chicken Farming Under the Spotlight The Oxford researchers point to the rapid expansion of global poultry farming as a possible factor behind the changing behavior of Campylobacter. Worldwide, the chicken population has increased approximately sevenfold since the 1960s, reaching around 31 billion birds . Large commercial poultry farms often house thousands of chickens in close proximity. According to the researchers, this creates ideal conditions for bacteria to spread rapidly from bird to bird. Wild birds can also introduce bacteria into commercial flocks, where the organisms may continue circulating and evolve over time. The researchers suggest these farms can effectively act as reservoirs where bacteria survive, multiply, and exchange genes. Growing Concerns About Antibiotic Resistance One of the study's most significant findings involves antimicrobial resistance. Scientists observed genetic changes that may allow Campylobacter to better survive antibiotic treatment. Antibiotic resistant bacteria are considered one of the biggest public health challenges worldwide because infections become more difficult to treat and may require stronger or less effective medications. Reducing unnecessary antibiotic use in both human medicine and agriculture has become a major priority for health authorities around the world. Is There a Link to Bowel Cancer? One aspect attracting attention is previous research suggesting Campylobacter could influence certain cancers. Earlier laboratory studies have found that toxins produced by specific Campylobacter strains may interact with existing bowel cancer cells. Researchers believe these toxins could activate biological pathways that encourage tumors to become more aggressive or spread more easily. Importantly, current evidence does not show that Campylobacter causes bowel cancer in healthy people . Instead, scientists are investigating whether infection may influence the progression of cancers that already exist. More clinical research is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn. Poultry Remains a Major Source of Infection Previous Oxford research found that approximately 80 percent of human Campylobacter infections in one region of England were associated with poultry meat. Some of those bacterial strains also showed resistance to commonly used antibiotics. Although poultry is considered the primary source, Campylobacter can also spread through: Contaminated water Unpasteurized milk Contact with infected animals Cross contamination in kitchens Rare person to person transmission Proper food handling remains one of the most effective ways to reduce infection risk. How to Reduce Your Risk Health authorities recommend several simple precautions when preparing poultry at home. These include: Cook chicken thoroughly until the internal temperature reaches safe levels. Avoid washing raw chicken, which can spread bacteria through water droplets. Use separate chopping boards for raw meat and ready to eat foods. Wash hands with soap after handling raw poultry. Clean kitchen surfaces and utensils after preparing raw meat. Refrigerate poultry promptly and follow storage instructions. These food safety practices significantly reduce the chance of infection. What the Researchers Say Professor Sam Sheppard, senior author of the study, said that industrial poultry farming has created one of the largest animal habitats on Earth, allowing bacteria that once circulated mainly among wild birds to establish themselves more successfully in commercial chicken populations. Lead author Oakem Kyne noted that understanding how farming practices influence bacterial evolution is important for reducing foodborne illness and slowing the development of antimicrobial resistance. The researchers emphasize that their findings should help improve disease prevention strategies rather than discourage poultry consumption altogether. The Bigger Public Health Picture Foodborne illnesses remain a significant global health issue. As food production systems become larger and more interconnected, scientists continue studying how agricultural practices affect the evolution of bacteria capable of infecting humans. The Oxford study adds to growing evidence that monitoring bacterial evolution in commercial farming environments is essential for protecting both animal and public health. Future research may help identify farming practices that reduce bacterial transmission while maintaining efficient food production. Consumers can also play an important role by following recommended food safety guidelines whenever preparing poultry at home. Conclusion The latest Oxford research highlights how changes in modern poultry farming may be influencing the spread and evolution of Campylobacter, one of the world's leading causes of bacterial food poisoning. Although the findings raise important questions about antibiotic resistance and food safety, they do not suggest that consumers should avoid eating chicken altogether. Instead, the study reinforces the importance of responsible farming practices, continued scientific monitoring, and safe food preparation. With proper handling and thorough cooking, the risk of Campylobacter infection can be greatly reduced while researchers continue investigating how agricultural systems shape the bacteria that affect human health. Source Kyne O. et al. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) , University of Oxford research on Campylobacter evolution in commercial poultry. Disclaimer This article is for informational and educational purposes only and should not be considered medical advice. It summarizes findings from scientific research and does not establish a direct cause and effect relationship between commercial chicken consumption and cancer. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional for medical concerns or food safety guidance.

title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
summary: Ollama now supports subagents and web search in Claude Code.
body_text: Ollama now supports subagents and web search in Claude Code. No MCP servers or API keys required. Get started ollama launch claude --model minimax-m2.5:cloud It works with any model on Ollama’s cloud. Subagents Subagents can run tasks in parallel, such as file search, code exploration, and research, each in their own context. Longer coding sessions stay productive. Side tasks don’t fill the context with noise. Some models will naturally trigger subagents when needed (minimax-m2.5, glm-5, kimi-k2.5), but you can force triggering subagents by telling the model to “use/spawn/create subagents” Example prompts: > spawn subagents to explore the auth flow, payment integration, and notification system > audit security issues, find performance bottlenecks, and check accessibility in parallel with subagents > create subagents to map the database queries, trace the API routes, and catalog error handling patterns Web search Ollama’s web search is now built into the Anthropic compatibility layer. When a model needs current information, Ollama handles the search and returns results directly without any additional configuration. Subagents can leverage web search to research topics in parallel and come back with actionable results. > research the postgres 18 release notes, audit our queries for deprecated patterns, and create migration tasks > create 3 research agents to research how our top 3 competitors price their API tiers, compare against our current pricing, and draft recommendations > study how top open source projects handle their release process, review our CI/CD pipeline, and draft improvements Recommended cloud models minimax-m2.5:cloud glm-5:cloud kimi-k2.5:cloud Learn more ollama launch for more integrations Claude Code with Ollama for basic setup Web search API for standalone usage

title: Stop Manually Data-Entering SAFEs: The AI-Native Approach to Equity Management
summary: Stop manually entering SAFEs into a spreadsheet. Discover how AI-native equity software automates your cap table tracking with zero data entry.
body_text: If you’re currently managing your startup’s equity on a spreadsheet, nobody can blame you. Excel and Google Sheets are great. They’re flexible, free, and great for financial forecasting. When you’re just setting up your corporate entity, tracking a couple of co-founder splits and an early advisor on a spreadsheet makes total sense. But as you scale, a subtle shift happens. You start raising capital via Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFEs). You issue an equity offer letter to a new engineer. You bring on a strategic advisor. Suddenly, your spreadsheet stops being a modeling tool and starts acting as a database . And that is exactly when things get dangerous. Because manually transcribing high-stakes legal PDFs into a manual grid in 2026 is an open invitation for expensive, catastrophic data errors. The Tipping Point: Where Spreadsheets (and Legacy SaaS) Break Most founders assume the natural upgrade path from a spreadsheet is to buy into the big brand cap table software platform. But when you look under the hood of those traditional platforms, you realize a frustrating truth: they still rely on the exact same manual data-entry workflows as your spreadsheet. The old process of logging a SAFE or an option grant looks like this: You close a SAFE on DocuSign (another SaaS bill). You open the finalized PDF document. You manually copy the Valuation Cap. You manually copy the Discount Rate. You manually type the investor’s full legal name and email address into your software database. If you misplace a decimal point, mix up a pre-money versus post-money cap, or mistype a name, your source of truth is broken. When it’s time to convert those SAFEs during a preferred priced round, a single manual entry error can alter your ownership percentages by hundreds of thousands of dollars. Why are founders paying legacy software companies thousands of dollars a year just to act as manual data-entry clerks? Enter the AI-Native Cap Table The modern tech stack has evolved, and equity management is finally catching up. At Mantle, we believe that software should do the heavy lifting, not the founder or an expensive team of back-office manual auditors. Instead of fighting your workflow, Mantle Equity uses an AI-native approach to turn your legal documents into a clean, automated system of record instantly. Here is how an AI-native equity workflow actually functions: 1. Document Extraction, Not Manual Typing With tools like Mantle’s AI Extract , you don’t type data into a database. You simply drag and drop your executed legal PDFs (like SAFEs or convertible notes) directly into the platform. AI Extract instantly reads the document and pulls out the investment amount, valuation caps, discount rates, and pro-rata rights with flawless accuracy. 2. Conversational Cap Table Assistance Need to check a metric or run a quick scenario? Instead of navigating complex software menus or writing custom spreadsheet formulas, you can interact with Mantle Clerk , your AI-powered equity copilot. You can ask natural questions like, “What is our current unallocated option pool?” or “Show me our top five shareholders after our last rolling SAFE note,” and get instant, accurate visual answers. 3. Open Data and Portability Legacy platforms thrive on data lock-in. They make it intentionally difficult to extract your data because they want to trap you in their ecosystem. Mantle is built entirely on the Open Cap Table Format (OCF) . This means your data is fully portable, compliant with modern legal tech standards, and easily readable by your legal counsel without requiring manual conversions. Watch our tactical session on How to Automate Your SAFE Fundraising Loop . Keep Your Spreadsheets for Modeling. Let AI Handle the Ledger. We aren’t here to tell you to delete Excel. Excel is a phenomenal sandbox for predicting the future, visualizing growth scenarios, and brainstorming hypothetical math. But when it comes to your company’s actual, legal source of truth, relying on manual data entry is a ticking regulatory time bomb. By upgrading to an AI-native infrastructure, you eliminate human error, bypass the boring administrative busywork, and ensure your company’s equity database updates itself flawlessly in the background. title: The Ultimate AI Hiring Assistant Crash Course for Restaurant Leaders [With Free Downloadable Resource]
summary: Explore how GenAI is reshaping restaurant hiring—from faster vetting to fewer no-shows. Including a free, data-driven eBook, The Landscape of AI in Hourly Recruitment.
body_text: So, you’re a restaurant or hospitality brand owner who wants to get on board with Artificial Intelligence? You’ve come to the right place. While Artificial Intelligence is the buzz word on everyone’s lips, it’s also a powerful tool slowly making its mark in restaurant operations. In fact, the current market valuation for restaurant AI is $9.68B , set to climb to $49B within the next 5 years. Despite this staggering growth, the restaurant industry continues to lag behind global usage rates of AI across all business sectors. At 47% , compared to an industry-wide 72% , the hospitality sector is slowly embracing AI at a year-over-year rate of 7% . But, operator sentiment is slowly warming, with 54% of surveyed operators believing that AI will positively impact restaurants. From the same survey, 94% agreed that AI is necessary to stay competitive. And given that challenges in recruiting and retaining hourly workers continue to plague 77% of restaurant operators, what better place is there to apply cutting-edge technology than in building cutting-edge teams? In this guide, we’ll walk you through the ways that Artificial Intelligence is the hiring assistant that you've been dreaming of. Make sure you scroll to the end for an exclusive eBook about The Landscape of AI. When we’re done, you’ll be ready to embrace the technology of the future and build the teams your brand deserves. Your Ultimate Hiring Assistant Before we discuss AI in any capacity, let's take a second to list out the hiring tasks that you'd like to pass off to an assistant. Having spoken to hundreds of restaurant General Managers and Operators at industry-leading brands like Tao Group Hospitality, Torchy's Tacos, and Another Broken Egg Cafe, the answer is clear: Admin work. From sifting through resumes to chasing down no-shows, manual hiring tasks eat up time you could spend mentoring your team and creating great guest experiences. In a survey by the Harvard Business Review, restaurant operators reported which tasks they wanted help with to streamline restaurant operations. At the top of the list were: - 46%: Applicant Screening & Assessment - 39%: Applicant Management & Communication - 36%: Data Analytics - 34%: Better Integration (with existing tools) - 33%: Real-Time Application Status Updates/Alerts It's clear that the restaurant industry needs to find a better way for GMs to handle tedious mundane hiring tasks. What Is AI? In order to assess what AI is best at, it's important to know what it is. Artificial Intelligence simulates human intelligence, using data and learning models to complete tasks that would typically require human cognition. Generative AI does all of the above, but also understands patterns and structures in data, using them to generate new, similar outputs. It's clear that Gen AI is more than capable of handling the tasks outlined above — and doing it with speed, at scale, and ensured quality. Sure, you could spend hours of time pouring through resumes to find your perfect match. And when your brand opens a new restaurant, you can do it again — and again. With Generative AI, you can trust that you are getting the best candidates for your brand. The technology is constantly refining and evolving according to your data, preference, and needs. It also keeps your hiring pipeline moving along on weekends or evenings, responding to candidates instantaneously. Read next → How Kava used AI to drive 3x more hiring wins What are the benefits of GenAI in hourly recruitment? According to Gartner’s 2024 Hype Cycle for Talent Acquisition: “GenAI built on top of Language Learning Models can enhance hiring manager efficiency, enhance talent attraction and engagement, and improve the quality of hires.” Here are some ways that GenAI benefits your restaurant hiring strategy. 1. Candidate Vetting at Scale Think about how many hours you spend combing through resumes to find the ideal candidate. How long does it take to get a conversation started, ask some qualifying questions, and schedule an interview? At scale, the time cost to hiring managers, GMs, and restaurant managers is exponential. And that’s not even taking into account the time spent trying to retain employees. Maybe you’re struggling with job hoppers, hourly workers who have moved from position to position multiple times within the past few months. Set up custom parameters to filter out candidates who have held multiple jobs in the past six months. Filtering with GenAI not only allows you to find the best talent, but you’ll also be able to minimize the chances that the candidate you hire will quit a month into the job. And if you want to get even fancier, consider AI-driven features like Dynamic Screening — that is, the ability to enforce stringent vetting criteria when you're shorter on interview hours. The beauty of AI is being able to customize it to your brand's nice-to-have's and must-have's. Take advantage of GenAI's data synthesis abilities and use it to help you find your perfect needle in the haystack. 2. Speedy Candidate Engagement ‍ Did you know that hourly candidates apply to an average of 14+ jobs in one sitting? And that they're most likely to accept the option that responds to them first? In the competitive game of restaurant and hospitality hiring, speed is key to securing the talent that you want. WeCruitr.io founder Jack Kelly writes , “The life of a headhunter is intensely competitive. They must race against time to find the best candidate before all of their competitors, or the company itself.” Speed the process up by engaging candidates right after they submit their application. This ensures that you stay top of mind and kicks off the hiring process ahead of your competitors. But what happens when an applicant hits submit at 2 a.m. in the morning? Or on a Saturday? Are you, the hiring manager, supposed to drop everything to strike up a conversation? After all, 38% of applicants apply “after hours." This number increases to 54% including nights and weekends. This is where Generative AI comes in. According to Gartner’s 2024 Hype Cycle report, “GenAI…has the potential to provide enhanced personalization in candidate UX and reduce recruiter intervention due to chatbot handoffs.” Set up a response system that triggers immediately after an application is received. This can come in the form of an email, chat bot, or, most effectively, a text message chain . Given that 75% of the restaurant workforce are Gen Z and Millenials, it's crucial to have a text-to-apply option. Create parameters for AI to handle it all for you. That way, you’ll wake up on Monday with a streamlined list of qualified candidates already scheduled to interview, not a mountain of unfiltered applications. And remember, time is money. Which leads us to… 3. Lower Cost Per Hire A speedier process means that you can shorten the life of your paid job listings. This significantly reduces ad spend on platforms such as Indeed, LinkedIn, and Glassdoor, where sponsored posts receive the most traffic. By utilizing GenAI, Tim Horton’s saw an 83% more efficient cost per hire and a 73% improvement in interview attendance rates. via LANDED 4. Job Listing Optimization In a landscape where job posting platforms are prioritizing sponsorships over organic posts , it’s important to make every listing count. Gartner reports: “Recruiters find Language Learning Model-enabled content creation attractive in recruitment as it enables them to create contextual recruitment content for candidates and employees.” Using GenAI to create job listing copy and content is a key way to optimize each post for the best candidates. Leverage existing data to see which posts have performed better than others and feed this information to the AI to craft the perfect description. GenAI can also be a powerful tool when it comes to multi-generational hiring. In today’s competitive hiring market, it’s not enough to have a single hiring strategy. Remember to customize your approach across all candidate verticals – after all, Gen Z resonate with different content than Boomers and Millennials do. For multinational franchises, another important candidate vertical is location. Certain wording may or may not resonate when placed into different geographic contexts. In order to maintain a constant stream of candidates, you’ll have to refine your approach for different populations. 5. Strong Employer Branding via Freepik Creating a strong employer brand is key to recruitment and retention. Let's face it – hiring isn't easy for anyone. And when candidates are submitting on average 14 applications at a time, it’s easy to feel like every submission is just another drop in a bucket. Use custom AI parameters to engage candidates in a way that acknowledges their efforts. This creates a foundation of empathy, understanding, and appreciation. Once employees begin their jobs, this will translate into a positive team culture that they’ll want to invest in for the long haul. Reduce Interview No Shows Improving the employee experience with AI-powered communication can also help minimize interview no-shows . Set up an interview reminder flow that pings each candidate before their interview. You can customize this cadence to a week, day, or even hour before. Assistant...or replacement? You may also be wondering... Is Generative AI going to replace human hiring managers and GMs? In short: no. As Sunkee Lee. Ph.D. and Associate Professor of Organizational Theory and Strategy at the Tepper School of Business, Carnegie Mellon University, writes: “By striking a harmonious balance between the capabilities of AI and the expertise of human decision-makers, organizations can truly unlock their potential in building strong, diverse, and high-performing workforces for the future.” Nobody in the restaurant industry is a stranger to teamwork — in fact, a single person trying to take on every responsibility in a restaurant would be a surefire recipe for disaster. Remember that AI is there to assist you , not take away your job. Even if it wanted to, it simply couldn't. At the end of the day, the restaurant industry is a people-first industry. Even if a candidate is perfect on paper, the only way to confirm they’ll be a great fit for your brand is to meet them in person, get a sense of their personality and approach, and to see them in action. AI ensures that the candidates who come in for an interview are the best ones that you should consider. But at the end of the day, it’s up to you to determine whether they’re a good fit for your brand. Ultimately, AI is a tool to help you save time and focus on what truly matters to your brand–mentoring your teams, connecting with customers, and creating an amazing guest experience. Our Generative AI reads through candidate resumes, dynamically vetting and adjusting conversation flows to provide a best-in-class recruitment experience — for you and your applicants. We respond to candidates instantly, answering their questions in real time. LANDED handles all of your additional vetting questions, ensuring that only top quality talent makes it to the interview round. And to get the best results, we combine cutting-edge GenAI with a 24/7 human support team. Your dedicated Client Strategist collaborates with you to optimize your hiring strategy. With decades of experience securing top hires for industry leading brands, they’ll assess your analytics to provide best practices and recommendations. title: Der Subunternehmer präferiert Abrechnung auf Stundenbasis - wie kann man dennoch zusammenfinden?
summary: Subunternehmer bevorzugen meist die Abrechnung auf Stundenbasis. Wir sprechen über Möglichkeiten, hier doch noch zusammen zu finden.
body_text: Für Subunternehmer ist grundsätzlich die Arbeit auf Stundenbasis kalkulierbarer, weil die genauen Gegebenheiten des Projekts nicht bis ins letzte Detail verstanden werden müssen und man unternehmerisch kein großes Risiko eingeht. Außerdem entfällt der initiale Aufwand der Angebotserstellung. Wir möchten im Folgenden dennoch auf ein paar Punkte eingehen, wie Sie es als Auftraggeber schaffen können, einen Nachunternehmer von dieser von ihm präferierten Abrechnungsart abzubringen und davon zu überzeugen, für Sie auf Werkvertrag-Basis zu arbeiten. ‍ 1. Vor Projektstart: Vertrauen schaffen Starten Sie nicht direkt mit Vertragsdetails oder insbesondere nicht einer sofortigen pauschalen Ablehung des Subunternehmers, wenn dieser anfängt, Ihnen eine Zusammenarbeit auf Stundenbasis vorzuschlagen. Prüfen Sie zunächst, ob der Subunternehmer fachlich und menschlich zu Ihrem Projekt passt. Informieren Sie sich vorab über Referenzen und Nachweise. CoCrafter bietet Ihnen dafür zum Beispiel eine super Grundlage, um genau dies vorab einzusehen und zu prüfen. Machen Sie sich also Gedanken, ob der Subunternehmer grundsätzlich fachlich und bzgl. Kapazität in der Lage wäre, Ihr Projekt durchzuführen. Wenn Sie dies sichergestellt haben, können Sie in den nächsten Absprache-/Verhandlungsschritt übergehen und überlegen, ob es denkbar wäre, eine Pauschale Teil-Vergabe des Projekts mit dem Nachunternehmer zu vereinbaren. Subunternehmer schätzen dabei logischerweise klare Zusagen, Verlässlichkeit und schnelle Kommunikation. Überlegen Sie hier also je nachdem, wie viele Nachunternehmer Sie potenziell verfügbar hätten, ob Sie solch einen Vorschlag machen möchten - oder dies nicht nötig haben. ‍ 2. Vertragsphase: Klarheit vor Komplexität Vermeiden Sie Missverständnisse schon beim Vertragsabschluss - weil Subunternehmer eben keine Juristen sind :) Verträge schlank halten: Ein kompakter Vertrag mit wenigen Seiten reicht häufig aus. Wichtige Punkte wie Leistung, Vergütung und Fristen sollten eindeutig formuliert sein. Besonders bei ausländischen Subs reduziert das Barrieren. → Tipp: Verwenden Sie einfache, klare Sprache. Lesen Sie hier, was in einen schlanken, rechtssicheren Nachunternehmervertrag gehört. Wichtig: Nehmen Sie sich unbedingt Zeit für ein 5-minütiges Telefonat, um dem Nachunternehmer den Vertrag zu erklären und diesen nicht wortlos auf eine Unterschrift zu drängen. Dies schafft Vertrauen und wird sich langfristig auszahlen! Probe-Modelle ermöglichen: Neue Subunternehmer sollten zuerst kleinere Teilaufträge übernehmen können. → Tipp: Arbeiten Sie schrittweise mit neuen Nachunternehmern und dokumentieren Sie klar, wer welche Arbeiten erledigt. CoCrafter ermöglicht Ihnen eine einfache Teilvergabe und Personaldokumentation. ‍ 3. Während des Projekts: Reibungslose Abläufe sichern Vermeiden Sie organisatorische Hürden und Konflikte durch klare Planung: Baustellenlogistik erklären: Frühzeitige Klärung logistischer Fragen vermeidet Frust und Unklarheiten. → Tipp: Kommunizieren Sie transparent, welche Bedingungen vor Ort gelten und auch was Sie als Auftraggeber dem Subunternehmer garantieren bzw. wie Sie ihn unterstützen werden. Verfügbarkeit sicherstellen: Sorgen Sie für durchgehende Arbeitsbedingungen. → Tipp: Besprechen Sie mit dem Bauleiter vorab mögliche Engpässe. Zahlungsmodalitäten klären: Vereinbaren Sie einfache und verständliche Zahlungsbedingungen sowie Einbehalte. → Tipp: Legen Sie individuell für jedes Projekt einen klaren Zahlungsplan fest. ‍ 4. Nach dem Projekt: Langfristig denken Bauen Sie gute Beziehungen gezielt aus: Feedback und Nachbesprechung: Nutzen Sie die Projektabschlussphase zur Verbesserung der Zusammenarbeit. Eine kurze Auswertung nach Projektabschluss hilft dabei, die Zusammenarbeit weiterzuentwickeln. → Tipp: Bitten Sie aktiv um Feedback und optimieren Sie die Abläufe gezielt. Seien auch Sie offen für Feedback vom Subunternehmer. Verlässliche Partner binden: Zuverlässige Subs sind wertvolle langfristige Partner. Wer solche Partner frühzeitig erkennt und pflegt, kann sie auch bei künftigen Projekten unkompliziert wieder einsetzen. → Tipp: Dokumentieren Sie mit CoCrafter, welche Subs zuverlässig arbeiten. So erleichtern Sie künftige Beauftragungen deutlich. ‍ Fazit Subunternehmer für eine Zusammenarbeit auf Werkvertragsbasis zu gewinnen, gelingt nicht durch Druck oder schnelle Verhandlungen – sondern durch Vorbereitung, Klarheit und Verlässlichkeit. Wer früh plant, transparent kommuniziert und gute Abläufe schafft, legt die Grundlage für langfristige und faire Partnerschaften. Tools wie CoCrafter erleichtern diese Schritte deutlich – und helfen Ihnen dabei, langfristige Partnerschaften aufzubauen. ‍ Interesse geweckt? Das klingt für Ihren Betrieb relevant? 👉 Kommen Sie jetzt auf uns zu uns wir zeigen Ihnen gern in einem 15-Minuten Video-Anruf, wie CoCrafter auch in Ihrem Unternehmen unterstützen kann. Hier Termin aussuchen. ‍

title: Cloud Vendors Make It Easy to Get In. They’re Counting on It Being Hard to Leave.
summary: Cloud vendors make it easy to get in. They're counting on it being hard to leave. Backblaze Universal Data Migration changes that.
body_text: You’ve done the storage evaluation. The per-terabyte price is right. The durability numbers check out. Compliance boxes are ticked. And still, the cloud migration project hasn’t been approved. That’s not a coincidence. The cloud storage industry has spent years competing on what happens after you’re already locked in: performance, redundancy, features. Almost nobody competes on what it costs to get there—or what it costs to leave. Migration friction isn’t an oversight. For most hyperscalers, it’s a business model. Why cloud migration projects stall before they start The business case for cloud storage usually looks solid on paper. Lower per-terabyte costs. Less hardware to maintain. A path off aging tape libraries and overloaded NAS environments. Then someone runs the actual migration math. Egress fees from the current provider. Data transfer charges. Migration software licenses. Professional services. Tape digitization. Internal engineering hours. Project coordination overhead. For a large dataset, those costs can erase years of projected storage savings before a single byte moves. Teams spend months building an approval-ready business case, only to find the upfront migration cost makes the model unworkable. The project stalls. Infrastructure the organization already knows is unsustainable stays in place. Modernization gets pushed to next quarter. This is where most cloud vendors win. The storage decision becomes moot if the organization can never afford to move. How egress fees trap organizations with their current provider By the time most IT teams discover what cloud egress fees actually cost, they’re already mid-negotiation with a new provider. The pricing model is deliberately asymmetric: getting data in is cheap, often free. Moving it out is where providers charge—and for multi-petabyte environments, those charges can run to hundreds of thousands of dollars before a migration has even started. Technically, the organization owns its data. Financially, moving it is a different question. This reframes the evaluation in a way that favors incumbents. The question stops being which platform best fits long-term needs and becomes whether the organization can afford to leave at all. Once you’re in a major cloud platform with a large archive, exit costs are a structural retention mechanism. Ask any prospective provider, early: what does it cost to leave? If they’re vague, that’s the answer. How long does a cloud data migration actually take? Cost gets scrutinized. Time usually doesn’t—until a migration is already underway and slipping. A large-scale migration means inventorying data and metadata, evaluating and procuring tooling, coordinating across vendors, monitoring transfer jobs, validating integrity at the destination, and troubleshooting the inevitable edge cases. For multi-petabyte environments, self-managed projects routinely stretch from months into years. Every quarter that drags on is a quarter the organization is paying to maintain infrastructure it’s already committed to replacing, while its engineering team runs a file-moving operation instead of working on anything strategic. The total cost of a slow migration almost always exceeds the initial estimate—and almost nobody builds that into the business case upfront. What actually goes wrong during cloud data migration Migration risk tends to be underestimated until something breaks. The core questions—will files transfer without corruption, will metadata survive intact, will dependent applications keep working—are harder to answer than they look for LTO tape archives that haven’t been accessed in years, NAS and SAN environments with proprietary metadata structures, media archives with irreplaceable assets, regulated content with chain-of-custody requirements, and datasets large enough that verification at scale is its own engineering problem. The cost of getting this wrong isn’t just the migration itself. Data loss, integrity gaps, or application failures discovered post-migration can be significantly more expensive than any egress fee. Validation and verification need to be designed into the plan before transfers start, not bolted on after something fails. Why most cloud providers leave migration to you Infrastructure teams evaluating cloud storage aren’t looking for a transfer tool. They want infrastructure modernized without burning their engineering team on a multi-year internal project. Predictable costs. A path to cloud that doesn’t require standing up a program management office just to move data. The standard provider response is documentation and an onboarding checklist. After that, you’re largely on your own. This isn’t an accident. Selling storage is straightforward. Owning migration means taking on cost, risk, and operational complexity that most providers would rather leave with the customer. The economics of the business favor making entry easy and exit expensive, with as little friction to growth as possible in between. Providers that treat migration as their problem to solve are a different category. They’re betting that making it genuinely easier to get to their platform is worth more than one-time migration revenue—because a customer who gets there successfully tends to stay. How Backblaze Universal Data Migration works We built Universal Data Migration because we kept seeing the same thing: organizations that had already decided to move to Backblaze B2 getting stuck on the migration itself. The technology decision was made. The budget was approved. The project just couldn’t get started. The program moves data from virtually any source—AWS S3, Microsoft Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage, Wasabi, NAS and SAN, file servers, LTO tape across all generations, physical hard drives, legacy archives—with Backblaze managing the process rather than handing the customer a tool and a runbook. The migration cost doesn’t have to be a reason the project stalls. That’s the point. Before you sign a cloud storage contract, ask these two questions The storage evaluation isn’t complete until you know what it costs to get there and what it costs to leave. Most providers make the second number hard to find. If you have to dig for egress pricing, or if a sales rep answers the exit question with “we’d work with you on that,” build the worst-case number into your model before signing anything. The right provider won’t make you ask. They’ll make migration part of the conversation from the start—because they’re confident enough in their platform to compete on the full picture, not just the monthly storage line. Have a migration project that keeps getting pushed? Talk to our team about what it would actually take to move your environment to B2.

body_text: View all news Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results 07/22/2026 Download (opens in new window) WILMINGTON, N.C., July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: LOB) (“Live Oak” or “the Company”) today reported second quarter of 2026 net income attributable to common shareholders of $34.7 million, or $0.74 per diluted common share. Live Oak’s performance in the quarter, compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, includes these notable items: Strong loan production of $1.55 billion accompanied by strong deposit growth of $712.5 million as of June 30, 2026, compared to March 31, 2026, with total assets growing by 4.8% and 16.0% to $16.04 billion as of June 30, 2026, compared to March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2025, respectively Net interest income increased 5.0% and 14.8% compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, respectively. Net interest margin increased 6 basis points during the second quarter of 2026 from 3.27% for the first quarter of 2026 to 3.33% and increased 5 basis points compared to the second quarter of 2025 Revenue (comprised of net interest income and noninterest income) increased 7.3% and 11.8% compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, respectively, and noninterest expense decreased 0.9% and 0.8% compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, respectively, which generated a 19.0% and 31.5% increase in pre-provision net revenue1 compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, respectively Provision expense for credit losses of $25.8 million for the second quarter of 2026, increased $5.7 million and $2.5 million compared to the first quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2025, respectively “Live Oak Bank’s performance in the second quarter includes several milestones worth highlighting,” said Live Oak Chairman and CEO James S. (Chip) Mahan III. “With $1.5 billion of loan originations, record Live Oak Express small dollar originations and strong checking balance growth, Live Oak layered another strong quarter of sustainable momentum across our core business. We are dedicated to serving American business owners with the capital and banking excellence they need, and our shareholders are seeing our path to success taking shape. It is an exciting time to be part of Live Oak’s journey, and I am incredibly proud of our teams." title: From connected customers to flexible homes: How Tibber and Enode are shaping the open energy ecosystem for the next grid
summary: For most of the power system's history, flexibility came from large industrial assets. That is changing. Electric vehicles, home batteries, solar panels, heat pumps and chargers are bringing flexibility into millions of homes. As these technologies become more common, households are becoming active participants in the energy system. The challenge is no longer simply supplying electricity. It is helping customers optimize how they use it, while building the foundation for a more flexible energy system. Unlocking flexibility requires more than connected devices. It requires connected homes, interoperable ecosystems and the ability to coordinate assets as part of a system. For Tibber, connected devices help customers save money, earn rewards, and get more value from the technologies they already own. For Enode, they are the foundation for residential energy flexibility. Together, Tibber and Enode are helping build a future where homes are not only consumers of electricity, but active participants in the next grid.
body_text: For most of the power system's history, flexibility came from large industrial assets. That is changing. Electric vehicles, home batteries, solar panels, heat pumps and chargers are bringing flexibility into millions of homes. As these technologies become more common, households are becoming active participants in the energy system. For energy retailers, this creates a new opportunity. The challenge is no longer simply supplying electricity. It is helping customers optimize how they use it, while building the foundation for a more flexible energy system. Tibber has built its platform around this idea. Through the Tibber app, customers can connect energy devices and automate how electricity is used in their homes. Charging can be scheduled automatically based on electricity prices, helping customers save money without actively managing their energy usage. As more customers connect devices, the opportunity expands beyond optimization. Connected homes become a foundation for residential energy flexibility. Turning connected devices into customer value For Tibber, connected devices are a core part of the customer experience. Customers use the Tibber app to automate energy usage based on dynamic electricity prices and system conditions. Features such as Smart Charging help EV owners charge when electricity is cheaper, while programs such as Grid Rewards allow customers to earn money by supporting the grid. The value is practical: customers save money, earn rewards, and gain a simpler way to manage energy at home. “Our customers care that their charging works, that automation behaves as expected and that they save and earn money. Reliable connectivity is what makes that experience possible at scale,” says Daniel Mata, Head of VPP Asset Growth at Tibber. “We’ve assessed this space thoroughly and explored multiple approaches, and chose to work with Enode to operate a selected part of this layer as part of our core platform. This allows us to expand device coverage and ensure reliable operation at scale, while keeping the experience simple for customers.” Connected energy devices also create monetary value for customers. Households using Smart Charging and Grid Rewards can significantly reduce charging costs while earning additional rewards for supporting the grid. In the Netherlands, top 25% of customers have reported up to 821 EUR savings per year , while users in Sweden experience 50% cheaper charging . Figure 1: Two examples from the Netherlands and Sweden, showing the value of connected energy devices. Both figures reflect the top 25% of customers using both Smart Charging and Grid Rewards. Connected energy devices are also becoming strategically important for energy retailers. Features such as Smart Charging create regular engagement with customers and establish a foundation for future energy services. As more households adopt EVs, batteries and other distributed energy resources, retailers that can successfully engage these customers are increasingly well-positioned to build differentiated energy products and flexibility programs. Open energy creates customer choice As more devices enter the home, customers should not be locked into isolated ecosystems. A household may own an EV from one manufacturer, a charger from another, and a battery from a third. Customers expect these technologies to work together and connect to the services that create the most value for them. This is where open energy becomes important. Open energy is built on trusted and standardized interfaces that allow devices, energy retailers and software platforms to work together reliably. It creates a foundation where customers can connect the devices they already own to the services they want to use, while giving retailers the ability to build products across a broad ecosystem of technologies. For customers, that means more choice. For energy companies, it creates a foundation for innovation. From connected devices to residential flexibility Connecting a device creates value. Coordinating multiple devices creates significantly more. A customer might start by connecting an EV for Smart Charging. Later, they may add a battery, solar panels, or a heat pump. Each asset contributes flexibility in a different way. An EV can shift charging. A battery can store and release energy. A heat pump can adjust consumption while maintaining comfort. For many retailers, flexibility programs have historically focused on individual devices. The next phase of the market will be different. As households adopt multiple energy assets, the opportunity shifts from optimizing individual devices to coordinating energy across the home as a whole. This is where residential energy flexibility emerges. The value comes not from individual devices acting independently, but from multiple assets working together as part of a coordinated system. Figure 2: The evolution of connected energy with Enode’s Energy Orchestration Platform Orchestrating assets across the home and grid To support this, Tibber works with Enode across a growing set of device integrations. Enode helps energy retailers connect, optimize and orchestrate distributed energy assets across the home and grid. For Tibber, Enode operates a selected part of this layer as part of Tibber's broader platform, helping expand device coverage while maintaining reliable operation across connected energy assets. This allows Tibber to focus on building great customer experiences while creating the foundation for future flexibility services. As more customers connect EVs, chargers, batteries and other energy devices, the challenge becomes larger than any individual integration. Success depends on the ability to coordinate assets reliably across homes and markets. What begins as connectivity becomes orchestration. What begins as one connected device grows into an important puzzle piece of a broader, open energy system. Building the next grid European energy markets are changing. The energy system is becoming more distributed. Unlocking flexibility requires more than connected devices. It requires connected homes, interoperable ecosystems and the ability to coordinate assets as part of a system. For Tibber, connected devices help customers save money, earn rewards, and get more value from the technologies they already own. For Enode, they are the foundation for residential energy flexibility. Together, Tibber and Enode are helping build a future where homes are not only consumers of electricity, but active participants in the next grid.
